notes.note: #2932 part 2 round 2: session-api.md replaced its compound-command limit under respondToRequest (a compound command with no signal about its parts is now a plain call; the invisible cases are listed). The ADR cites the session API only as the current orchestration surface; its decisions do not concern approval grants.

#2932 part 2 round 2 (owner decision): claudeAskEscalates now treats subcommandResults on Bash and PowerShell as a plain call unless classifierApprovable is set, matchedAskRule is present or decisionReason has text; the blocked-path, directory-suggestion, sandbox-override and ask-flag signals still apply through toolRequestEscalates. Rewrote the type bullets, corrected the sentence that said a nested safety check cannot be ruled out (classifier_approvable absent rules it out), and replaced the 'compound commands prompt' limit with the accepted gap: an exact ask rule on one part and a part's non-safety other warning are not on the request. Added a third invisible case found by reading the 2.1.278 Bash permission code: in an && or ; command with two or more parts needing approval, the engine keeps only addRules rules from the parts' suggestions (capped at five) and no blocked path, so a part's addDirectories suggestion for a write outside the working directories is dropped; a pipeline keeps the parts' suggestions whole, and a lone asking part is returned with its own blocked path. Stated that these shapes were read in the binary, not captured live. Tap paragraph: a replay is read only on the response to the SDK's initialize request (recognised from the SDK's stdin writes) and conflicting records for one request id read as missing; checked against claude-permission-frames.ts, claude-code-spawn.ts and their tests, including the real-SDK test. Each clause of the new rule was fault-injected against the shared and adapter tests.
